findings.rationale: First-model authorization treats receipt fields, a merely 64-character sha256 value, and caller-supplied identity booleans as proof. require_first_model_authorization then accepts a minimal mapping without recomputing stage receipts. controlled_decision similarly trusts stage strings, machine-gate booleans, audit_complete, and summary counts; authorize_release accepts a minimal PASS mapping. These entry points can authorize model execution or release without authentic, hash-bound evidence.
findings.required_action: Replace caller-supplied booleans and summary mappings with verification of exact candidate-bound artifacts, recomputed content hashes, trusted issuer signatures, source/environment/model digests, and immutable stage receipts. Authorization entry points must reject hand-constructed decision objects.
findings.title: Model-run and release guards accept caller-authored success objects

findings.rationale: The importer never recomputes manifest entry hashes, sizes, or the aggregate bundle digest. Its authority receipt contains only self-asserted identities and an unverified signature-reference hash; archive replay and finding evidence hashes are format-checked but not bound to replay/evidence files. A supplied transcript is byte-hashed but not shown to be an archive replay or independent review. The importer can consequently emit INDEPENDENT R0-R2 stage receipts without a trust anchor or substantive replay proof.
findings.required_action: Before import, validate the manifest schema and boundaries, recompute every entry and aggregate, verify a trusted issuer's cryptographic authority signature, bind replay and finding hashes to supplied files and exact archive/member checks, and validate the response against a role-appropriate schema.
findings.title: The bootstrap importer can mint unauthenticated independent stage receipts

findings.rationale: If all three stage decisions are ACCEPTED while bootstrap_policy_disposition is REVISE_R0_R2_AND_DO_NOT_AUTHORIZE_ANY_MODEL_CALL, import_review still sets independent_acceptance to true and emits accepted stage receipts. Only the textual status and next action change. Neither response.schema.json nor the importer imposes the required conditional relationship.
findings.required_action: Make the dispositions conditional: the REVISE/no-call disposition must require all R0-R2 decisions to be REVISE and must emit no accepted receipts; accepted receipts may be emitted only for the new-candidate bootstrap disposition with all other authority checks satisfied.
findings.title: The no-model-call policy can coexist with accepted stage receipts

findings.rationale: validate_claim_request does not require the evidence record's candidate_id to equal candidate.3. inventory_sha256 is only syntax-checked. Gate receipts are checked for path/hash and agreement with the record's candidate string, but the receipt file is not parsed to prove the named gate, stage, candidate, or acceptance. A cross-candidate record with self-labeled gate IDs can therefore satisfy the validator when quality_outcome is TARGET_MET.
findings.required_action: Require candidate.3 explicitly, recompute and compare its canonical inventory root, parse each gate receipt against a strict schema, verify gate/stage/candidate/evidence class and trusted authority, and reject reused files masquerading as multiple gates.
findings.title: Claim requests are not bound to candidate.3 inventory or gate semantics

findings.rationale: Reconciliation defines completeness solely as no unfinalized attempts. A finalized planned call with no native ID is therefore complete; failed calls are counted as attempts rather than actual calls; one provider-terminal boolean and one usage object can mark multiple native IDs complete; schema and success invariants are not revalidated; and MCP mutation is permitted after FINALIZED. Runtime MCP IDs are recorded only after parsing the structured response, while error/parse paths finalize without the native ID. Cost fields are also not semantically validated. The retained five-call pre-ledger disclosure is honest, but the replacement ledger does not guarantee future all-attempt accounting.
findings.required_action: Use per-native-call acceptance and terminal events journaled before parsing, make FINALIZED immutable, validate every snapshot against the schema and legal transition invariants during reconciliation, count calls rather than attempts, and classify missing planned IDs/terminals as unknown rather than complete.
findings.title: Ledger reconciliation can declare incomplete or mutated call histories complete

findings.rationale: The benchmark project and lock resolve milai-runtime from editable ../../runtime, but no runtime tree exists in the bundle or candidate source inventory. The seven-entry runner/helper closure includes two absent scripts, including the closure builder and BFCL worker runner. Representative bundled tests import absent scripts, integrations, and evals.agent_integration. Hash-only captures and executable identities cannot replay the asserted fresh install and 193-test result.
findings.required_action: Freeze milai-runtime as a content-addressed wheel or complete tree, include it and every runner/helper/imported implementation in one source root, materialize sanitized install/test transcripts, bind the upstream checkout and executable/image identities, and independently rebuild from those exact bytes.
findings.title: The claimed R2 worker closure omits mutable and execution-critical source bytes

findings.rationale: R3 requires a 24/24 T2 model smoke, while the frozen authorization rule requires R3 ACCEPTED before any model request. The smoke preflight always passes receipts=[] and does not consume importer output, so even external R0-R2 receipts have no wired path. Candidate.3 cannot reach R3 without violating its own rule.
findings.required_action: Keep candidate.3 model calls denied. After R0-R2 remediation and independent review, freeze a new candidate with a narrowly scoped R0-R2 control-path bootstrap rule permitting exactly the ledgered 24-call T2 smoke under frozen identities and no test access; require R3 acceptance before every other model run.
findings.title: The first-model policy has no reachable compliant R3 transition

findings.rationale: build_quality_gate skips knowledge_update or temporal thresholds when a category is absent, requires only that confirmation dev be nonempty, and accepts topology completion, ledger completeness, threshold freezing, and human approval as booleans. Thus a one-case confirmation set with missing required strata and no bound human receipt can set full_test_authorized=true.
findings.required_action: Bind both dev sets to preregistered case manifests and minimum denominators, require both mandated ability strata, consume the validated topology and ledger receipts by hash, and verify a signed human test-access approval artifact rather than a boolean.
findings.title: The quality gate can authorize full-test access without required strata, denominator, or approval receipt

findings.rationale: The gate enforces 216 total rows and 80 multi-turn rows but not exact supported-single-turn and no-call denominators or a case-to-category manifest. Category, pass, capability, and dependency-closure values are caller-supplied, while dependency hashes are only syntax-checked. Reclassification or unsupported summary construction can change denominators without detection.
findings.required_action: Bind all 216 case IDs, categories, languages, expected denominators, adapter, worker, ledger, and dependency files to a frozen manifest and derive the gate from verified per-case receipts.
findings.title: The BFCL gate does not bind category labels and exact denominators to a frozen dataset

findings.rationale: build_serving_gate accepts caller-created cell mappings and does not verify schema, candidate, workload-contract digest, attempt ledger, source/model identity, or cross-cell attempt/native-ID uniqueness. Model-round and MCP-round counts are not constrained by tier or native-ID count. Reused IDs or hidden topology differences can therefore pass the author gate.
findings.required_action: Build cells directly from a globally reconciled attempt ledger, verify workload and candidate/source/model hashes, enforce global ID uniqueness and tier-specific round topology, and validate raw per-attempt trace/resource receipts before summarization.
findings.title: Serving summaries are not bound to workload, ledger, or global request identity

findings.rationale: The prompt says Codex is advisory only, cannot satisfy R0 archive replay, and cannot accept stages. The response schema nevertheless requires reviewer_role_separated=true, HUMAN or INDEPENDENT evidence, authorized protected-archive access=true, and only ACCEPTED/REVISE stage decisions. The importer also requires archive access even for a REVISE response. An honest AI-only closed-bundle response cannot conform.
findings.required_action: Separate an AI advisory schema with explicit no-authority and no-archive values from a human promotion schema. Only the latter may carry signed acceptance and authorized archive replay.
findings.title: The bundled Codex prompt has no truthful schema-conforming advisory response

findings.rationale: The claim matrix records DG10-R2 as NOT_STARTED, while the worker-closure report, direct-binding report, and engineering status describe R2 as AUTHOR_CANDIDATE. The contract validator does not reconcile these artifacts, and the smoke preflight reads the stale claim-matrix state.
findings.required_action: Use one candidate-bound append-only stage ledger and require every report, validator, and authorization preflight to consume and cross-check the same receipt hashes and current state.
findings.title: Candidate.3 R2 has conflicting stage states across frozen artifacts
